title: 2020 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
claims: The 2020 guidelines are aligned with the International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation and emphasise early recognition and activation of the chain of survival.
Unresponsiveness with absent or abnormal breathing is the recognition trigger for bystander action in adults.
The guidelines recommend immediate emergency calling and rapid access to an automated external defibrillator by trained or untrained bystanders.
During manual CPR for an average adult, compress to a depth of at least 2 inches (5 cm) while avoiding excessive depths greater than 2.4 inches (6 cm).
In adult victims of cardiac arrest, compressions are performed at a rate of 100 to 120 per minute.
When two or more rescuers are available, switch chest compressors approximately every 2 minutes (or after about 5 cycles of 30:2) to prevent decreases in compression quality.
Before an advanced airway is placed, CPR is performed at 30 compressions to 2 breaths; compression-only CPR is appropriate when lay rescuers are untrained or unwilling to give respirations.

The adult cardiac arrest chain proceeds through recognition and activation of the emergency response system, CPR, defibrillation and post-ROSC supportive care; early defibrillation with concurrent high-quality CPR is critical for VF or pulseless VT.
